correctness.rationale: For every positive integer dimension, real exponent strictly between one and infinity, and positive radius, strict convexity makes the metric minimizer unique. A sign reduction and active KKT conditions establish a universal threshold independent of the exponent. Piecewise-affinity with active Jacobian given by the signed mean-subtraction projector proves the global Lipschitz upper bound; a full-dimensional cell exists for each active cardinality and realizes the matching lower bound. The two-coordinate mean-subtraction map has norm one, and every such map is an orthogonal projector in Hilbert geometry. In the three-coordinate setting, shifting the zero-mean vector with entries one, one, and minus two along the constant direction proves strict expansion at every non-Hilbert exponent. For the three-coordinate fourth-power norm, the zero-sum quartic identity, complete Lagrange stationary-point classification, Vieta argument, and weighted Hölder bound prove the radical value; transpose duality supplies the conjugate exponent. A standalone verifier was successfully run from its actual package path and checks identities and active-cell realization. General dimensional and exponent conclusions follow from the proof, not finite experiments; zero radius, endpoint exponents and weighted norms are excluded.

originality.rationale: The 2008 primary source proves Euclidean soft thresholding but not the simultaneous non-Euclidean metric-projection property, the sharp cellwise global Lipschitz characterization, the iff dimension/exponent criterion, or the exact fourth-power dimension-three constant. The 2014 primary source addresses minimal linear hyperplane projection constants, not the nonlinear nearest-point map. Searches of indexed findings across the object, its aliases, the central matrix, and the numeric value found no stated or dominating implication. The elementary threshold equation is not itself counted as novel. Unindexed older operator-norm formulas and uninspected related papers remain risks, so these searches are evidence of noncoverage in inspected records, never a proof of priority.
residual_risks: The p-independent soft-threshold observation is an elementary consequence of KKT conditions and may have appeared in optimization texts not indexed by the checked search; novelty rests on the complete sharp Lipschitz theorem and dimensional/exponent boundary.
A historical exact induced-norm formula for the three-coordinate centering projector could predate this work; even if so, the nonlinear-projection connection requires comparison.
Results available only through abstracts or unindexed material may imply part of the theorem; searched absence is not absolute uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: The cross-polytope is the canonical sparse-approximation constraint, for which global robustness of the nearest-point map in non-Euclidean coordinate geometries is mathematically natural. The result determines the exact all-dimensional sensitivity in terms of canonical finite linear projection norms, gives a necessary-and-sufficient nonexpansiveness criterion, identifies the smallest dimension where the Hilbert intuition fails, and computes its first sharp non-Hilbert modulus in radicals. This is a structural all-dimensions classification rather than just restating soft thresholding or an arbitrary numeric constant. A small numerical excess over 1 is substantive because it separates the two regimes sharply; no unsupported applications or new general downstream theorem are asserted.
